items.title: Wallace Davenport Interview, 1975-05-15
items.q: They just, like you told me many times, they're just looking at it as a gig.

ctx.x: Some of them. Some of them. Now, New Orleans musicians, yeah. But now a lot of guys wonder why I hide orange and a loss. As much as I do. But whenever I tell them to do it, they'll hide me. They'll do it. They'll do it. They'll do it. They'll do it.

They'll do it. They'll do it. They'll do it. They'll do it. What happens, I think, is that fellas like that look at you as the leader of the band. And the musicians who want to, what you tell them to, don't seem to realize that. That you hired them and you're the leader and you're supposed to play the way you want them to play. They just, like you told me many times, they're just looking at it as a gig. That's right.

Now, if somebody hires me to play with them down, whatever they tell me to do, I'm going to do that. If I figure I'm not going to do that, I can't do it. I won't accept the job. They want you to come home.
